subject: Emirates NBD
method: desk research of public sources only: bank and vendor press releases, trade press, vendor customer stories, public job adverts. No scanning, probing or non-public data was used.
status: outside-in baseline. It is NOT a CBOM: public sources do not disclose algorithms, keys, certificates or HSMs.

confidence_key.high: published by the bank or the vendor itself (press release / customer story)
confidence_key.low: third-party aggregator, job advert or undated page; use only as a lead to verify

currency_rule: Dates are publication dates; a disclosed product may since have been replaced. Treat dated disclosures as 'was deployed' and confirm current state with the bank.

organisation_profile.detail: Leading banking group in the MENAT region; presence in 13 countries; over 20 million customers.
Liv. (digital-only bank); API developer portal for corporate clients.
Emirates Islamic Bank went live on Finacle in 2016 (first Islamic site for that platform).
A bank job advert cites 853 branches and 4,213 ATMs/SDMs across the group.
Singapore (Nov 2018), UK (Jul 2019), Saudi Arabia (phase 3, Jan 2020); target of one platform for all entities by end-2020.

disclosures.name: Infosys Finacle (EdgeVerve)
disclosures.disclosed: Finacle used at home and across international entities; migration of all entities to one updated platform; award for core implementation (2020).

disclosures.name: TCS BaNCS for Payments
disclosures.disclosed: Selected as core payments platform to standardise payments across India, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Singapore, UK and UAE.

disclosures.name: Intellect Design Arena
disclosures.disclosed: Technology selected to overhaul wholesale/transaction banking as part of an AED 1 billion digitisation commitment.

disclosures.name: Calypso (treasury)
disclosures.disclosed: End-to-end upgrade consolidating treasury products into a single core system across markets.

disclosures.name: Pine Labs Credit+
disclosures.disclosed: Partnership to deliver in-store and online merchant acquiring solution.

disclosures.name: Silent Eight
disclosures.disclosed: AI and machine-learning platform to automate screening alert disposition; proof of value on the bank's screening alerts.

disclosures.name: Microsoft 365 Copilot, GitHub Copilot X, ChatGPT use cases
disclosures.disclosed: Announced July 2023; 'more than a thousand developers' on Copilot X; hackathon with McKinsey and QuantumBlack.

disclosures.name: OpenAI models
disclosures.disclosed: Reported as first MENA bank to use OpenAI sovereign AI infrastructure, connecting models to internal systems and APIs.

disclosures.name: Cloudera / Hadoop; Bloomberg; SAP
disclosures.role: Data platform; market data; enterprise apps
disclosures.disclosed: Listed by a procurement-research aggregator as detected products. Not confirmed by the bank here.

disclosures.name: API banking platform
disclosures.disclosed: API developer portal described as the region's most comprehensive; vendor not named.

disclosures.name: NCR (ATM estate)
disclosures.disclosed: Chosen as unified end-to-end self-service vendor; APTRA software; Windows 7 platform at the time of the 2014 announcement.
disclosures.currency_note: treat as 'was deployed'; confirm current state with the bank

disclosures.name: Dell PowerMax
disclosures.disclosed: Customer story: bank's core runs on PowerMax; 30% data-centre cost reduction; response times down to 1 ms.

disclosures.name: VMware
disclosures.disclosed: Trend Micro story states the IT environment is VMware.
disclosures.currency_note: treat as 'was deployed'; confirm current state with the bank

disclosures.name: In-house private cloud
disclosures.disclosed: Bank launched own private cloud, claimed as a regional banking first; underlying vendors not named in the retrieved text.

disclosures.name: du Tier III data centres
disclosures.disclosed: du hosts the bank's first third-party data centre and a further Tier III data hall in Dubai (announced Oct 2023).

disclosures.name: Moro Hub (DEWA)
disclosures.disclosed: Moro Connect cloud contact-centre built on Avaya OneCloud for the bank.

disclosures.name: Microsoft Azure; AWS
disclosures.disclosed: Azure powers Liv.; AWS used for ML, analytics, IoT and NLP in retail banking.

disclosures.name: Cisco + SONiC SDN fabric
disclosures.disclosed: Job advert for a Lead Technology Engineer to build and maintain an 'ENBD SDN-Fabric' using Enterprise SONiC and legacy networking; stack described as Cisco and SONiC.
disclosures.currency_note: job advert shows practices at the time of posting and may describe a specific team, not the whole bank

disclosures.name: IPsec, ACLs, routing authentication
disclosures.disclosed: Job advert lists network-security responsibilities including IPsec, ACLs and routing protocol authentication across bank data centres, server rooms and IDFs (owned or rented).
disclosures.currency_note: job advert shows practices at the time of posting and may describe a specific team, not the whole bank

disclosures.name: du (voice)
disclosures.disclosed: du provides data-centre hosting; du also launched 'Next Gen Voice' cloud-native communications platform with the bank (per aggregator).

disclosures.name: Avaya / Moro Connect
disclosures.disclosed: Long-standing Avaya relationship; cloud CCaaS delivered through Moro Hub in 2021.

disclosures.name: Trend Micro Deep Security
disclosures.disclosed: Customer story: in use about five years at the time, with plan to extend to the VMware platform.
disclosures.currency_note: treat as 'was deployed'; confirm current state with the bank

disclosures.name: Data443 Risk Mitigation
disclosures.disclosed: Multi-year subscription agreement spanning the bank's technology landscape, supporting a 'cloud first' migration of data and users.

crypto_siting.basis_for_inference: Core and payments platforms are disclosed [2][3].
crypto_siting.question_to_confirm: Which HSMs and key hierarchies protect core and payments? Which TLS versions between tiers?
Current ATM software/OS, key-loading method, and migration plan for terminal keys.
Who holds the keys for each cloud workload? Are customer-managed keys used?
How are DC-to-DC and DC-to-branch links encrypted?

crypto_siting.basis_for_inference: Job advert cites IPsec and routing authentication [19].
crypto_siting.question_to_confirm: IKE version, DH groups, and authentication method for all VPNs.

crypto_siting.basis_for_inference: API portal and OpenAI integration disclosed [12][25].
crypto_siting.question_to_confirm: Where are API signing keys held? How are AI connector secrets managed?

crypto_assets_typically_present: encryption of data at rest where the product applies it
crypto_siting.question_to_confirm: Which datasets are encrypted by these products and with which keys?

unverified_claims.statement: ENBD ran a quantum key distribution (QKD) pilot with a Toshiba system between two Dubai branches.
unverified_claims.treatment: could not be confirmed by the bank or Toshiba; treat it as a question to ask the bank, not as fact

gaps.statement: No public source gives ENBD's cryptographic algorithms, key lengths, certificate inventory, PKI, HSM vendor or TLS configuration. A CBOM cannot be completed from public data.
Dated items (NCR 2014, Trend Micro, VMware) may no longer reflect the estate.
Aggregator data (Cloudera, Bloomberg, SAP) [20] is unconfirmed.
Job adverts show practices at the time of posting and may describe a specific team, not the whole bank.
Network, firewall, SIEM/SOC, identity, PAM and HSM vendors are absent from public sources. Do not assume any.

data_requests.item: HSM inventory: vendor, model, firmware, partitions, key hierarchies, FIPS 140 level, which applications use each.
PKI: internal and external CAs, hierarchy depth, signature algorithms, certificate templates, lifetimes, revocation method.
Certificate inventory for internet-facing, internal, mobile-app, API and device certificates, with key type and size.
TLS and SSH configuration baselines per tier (load balancers, API gateways, middleware, databases), including minimum versions and cipher suites.
Network crypto: IPsec/IKE parameters, site-to-site and partner VPNs, wireless authentication (802.1X / EAP method), routing authentication.
Payment and card crypto: PIN/key management, key-exchange methods for ATMs and terminals, card-scheme and interbank connectivity, message signing.
Core and database encryption: transparent data encryption, tokenisation, backup encryption, and who holds the keys.
Cloud key management: KMS or BYOK/HYOK arrangements for each cloud and hosted facility, with key location and rotation.
Software supply chain: crypto libraries and versions per application (SBOM), code-signing keys, and CI/CD secrets handling.
Vendor contracts and roadmaps: each vendor's PQC readiness statement and the date they will support NIST FIPS 203/204/205.
Data-retention classes: which data must stay confidential for 10+ years (the 'harvest now, decrypt later' exposure).
